title: Thoughts on AI slop
author: International_Back30
selftext:
So my thoughts on why indie developers are hit hard by AI development and the big companies are not.

The main reason I see it is because the big companies have all the good practices in place: automated testing and high QC. 

Solo devs do not need to follow these rules, so anyone can release anything. That doesn't mean any indie dev will release poor content, but it does mean someone with little experience can release poor-quality content.

This is what tarnishes solo Devs. They may be the best developer but because AI is mentioned they are put in the same bucket. It's unfortunate but the way of the world.

comments.author: Stinky_You
comments.body: "This is what tarnishes solo Devs" -no it's not. your post hits like a defensive rant for people not liking your content.

replies.author: romansamurai
replies.body:
I’m thinking what tarnishes solo devs is the “one prompt” that “vibe coders” out there telling Claude to “make me a game about..:” and putting no other thought into it. No balancing and no quality control. 

That plus all the ones just cloning other games hoping to make a quick buck.

replies.author: PaintingThat7623
replies.body:
I don't understand why people judge ai game dev based on 1 prompt 1 shot games that are made as experiments, sort of benchmarks of what AI can do.

Can't you just... prompt more? Design something innovative, fun and polished? My game is on - roughly - prompt nr. 3000\~.

replies.author: romansamurai
replies.body:
Experiments are fine my friend. Those experiments going into steam and App Store for money is the problem.

My GDD is almost 400 pages and I wrote most of it last year myself. My version update history is also getting into mid 200s pages. I’m with you.

replies.author: PaintingThat7623
replies.body: Right? Be an architect and interior designer. Let robots carry the bricks.

replies.author: romansamurai
replies.body:
100%. I don’t even look at myself as a coder or asset designer or vibe coder anymore even tho i learned blender and unity just for my game over the last year. 

We are directors. Which encompasses everything from art to assets to coding to story to everything else. 

We have a team working under us and we review everything and make decisions dozens of times a day. 

What AI allows us is the ability to do this without having millions of dollars to bankroll our own indie game company with a dozen employees doing all this. 

At least that’s how I look at it myself. Every single thing Claude does has my stamp on it whether it’s touch up, review or just simple ok.

replies.author: PaintingThat7623
replies.body:
>What AI allows us is the ability to do this without having millions of dollars to bankroll our own indie game company with a dozen employees doing all this.

My game is basically AA quality. I still can't believe it. It would've taken couple of years of work of 5+ professionals to achieve what I achieved in 4 months by myself.

Let's do the math. Say, 5000$ x 5 people x 50 months. That's 1,250,000$. Even if I'm off ten times and it would be "just" 125,000$ - like...

I paid about a thousand bucks. What a time to be alive.

replies.author: romansamurai
replies.body: 100% bro. Get your fucking imagination out there. Fuck yes.

replies.author: Stinky_You
replies.body: yeah exactly, you and the other guy have a lot of good points. glad I'm not the only one thinking about this stuff.

replies.author: International_Back30
replies.body:
Hey mate, I'm not concerned about anything I've made but more a reaction to what I've read on here. I completely understand what you are saying. 

What I'm trying to say is a good piece of software or game should always go through the same level of testing and the final result will be subject to those critiques. 

Unfortunately there's the opportunity to make something very easily without the same level of checks.

replies.author: Stinky_You
replies.body:
Good software and bad software existed long before AI, slop and cash grabs have existed since the olden days, and I'm not being antisemitic. I disagree about limiting peoples creative freedom. There are people buying all sorts of garbage out there. what you want to do is set publishing standards to something that is at your level of competency to eliminate competition. Smart, but that's a hard pass from me. AI is helping me to learn a lot before I'd even consider putting something on the market, if other people want to skip that step -let them.

edit: To add, I'm not buying any game until i see in-game footage, AI use or otherwise.

replies.author: International_Back30
replies.body: I think we agree. You make some good points.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
I think people are just looking for something to blame, “people hate my game because I used some AI,” not considering that the game could just be not fun, or it could look unappealing, or have all sorts of other problems. 

If you want to do better—spend more time on quality control and polish. Watch people play your game. Collect feedback.

comments.author: NegativePoetry1561
comments.body:
Alright, I hear what you say, but let me give you a little insight into the BIG Companies’ practices.

In a time long ago where Games came on Disc, Floppy or Cartridges, there were big and plentiful Test departments, the played games tirelessly to find all the bugs they could. They would be classed as A, B, C or D class bugs. A class being like a crash or game stopping bug and a D class bug being like a misspelled word. In those days the Games had to be as close to perfect as Humanly possible because once it was on that disc that was it, no going back!

When Digital products came along, that all changed a bit, test departments were cut down dramatically, often from 100+ people strong to like 5 that worked directly with the dev team side by side. Because bugs could be fixed after release with patches.

So in reality an Indie Dev has about the same chances to test and fix bugs as a BIG Company nowadays. They might even have few bugs because they are the only one working on the code, so it will be cleaner and more structured, depending on coding experience.

As for AI, I really hate that people put down AI so much, AI is still just an assistant, if you don't know what you want and are able to tell the AI exactly what you want you get what a lot of people might call "Slop", but, if you really know how to talk to AI, you can get it to write super clean, structured, secure code. The same goes for Art Assets. It's basically called Prompt Engineering which is becoming a job in it's self nowadays. There are actually positions available in big and small companies for skilled AI users.

I hope that one day "soon" people are gonna stop hating on AI Developers. Instead look forward to some of the cool shit they are gonna create. And let's face it Crap Games, have been around for the last since gaming began, so there will always bee crap games and good games, maybe now more crap that good, but it's still worth all the crap, if one great games comes from it! Or someone brings back on game from the past that makes people smile!

replies.author: International_Back30
replies.body:
Completely agree! For many years people have made amazing games and god awful games. Hate the game if it's a bad game, love the game if you love it. 

That's what reviews are for.

replies.author: romansamurai
replies.body: Exactly. Talented people, people with vision and those like me without either but who really want to create a good and quality game will be able to do with AI what they couldn’t do before because of finances and other constraints. Slop is slop. Eventually this will all settle down and games created with AI will be given the same considerations as those before.

replies.author: International_Back30
replies.body: You've hit on something that's potentially important. Finances. It's not financially viable for a solo Dev to use an artist. They are simply too expensive. It doesn't make sense.

replies.author: romansamurai
replies.body: Yup. I’ve looked at fiverr for to have someone to go over the stuff I made on blender and touch it up, it’s so expensive. Fresh 3d assets are $200 a pop.  It’s prohibitively expensive for a person without someway to bankroll it.

replies.author: International_Back30
replies.body:
Same experience here. I've looked at fiverr to produce 2D assets. It's not viable. I've purchased stuff from unity asset store which works for some things but not everything. 

As it happens my wife has a diploma in art and general illustration. So we're in the process of teaching her how to translate her skills from pen and paper to digital art.

comments.author: taisui
comments.body: Slop is slop, made by AI or meatbag, same

replies.body: I think you missed counted. It's only 274,922 times.

comments.author: International_Back30
comments.body:
I've got 30+ years of development. Mostly as a combination of c# and oracle DBA. I've had many years of satisfaction developing software for various companies. It's a been a blast. However, using AI has sparked my interest again. For many years the kick from developing software has always been lots of fun but seeing the potential of developing with AI is another level of satisfaction. 

I really enjoy it, but it doesn't stop me making high quality software.
